items.title: Signed-log target transform
items.spec: In fit_predict, replace y with z = sign(y) * log1p(|y|) before the stack is trained (the oof loop, meta Ridge target and base_predict all see z). Invert the final prediction with sign(p) * expm1(|p|) before returning it. Leave the rest of the pipeline unchanged, so the descriptor, Tanimoto and RBF members all train on the transformed scale. The meta-learner is fit on transformed oof predictions, and the inversion happens only at the end.

items.title: Winsorise extreme training targets
items.spec: Before training, clip the training targets to their 1st and 99th percentiles computed on train_y: y_c = np.clip(y, np.percentile(y, 1), np.percentile(y, 99)). Use y_c everywhere y is used inside fit_predict, including the oof loop and the final base_predict call. Test predictions are not clipped. This is a single line added after y is cast to float64.

items.title: Largest-fragment and salt stripping before featurising
items.spec: Add a helper that converts each SMILES to a canonical form with the largest organic fragment kept: parse with Chem.MolFromSmiles, split with rdkit.Chem.rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser, and neutralise with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Apply this helper once to train_smiles and test_smiles at the top of fit_predict, and use the cleaned SMILES for featurize, desc_vector and the Murcko scaffold groups. Keep the original order and length. Fall back to the input SMILES if parsing fails.

items.title: Crippen logP and TPSA as a small physchem block
items.spec: Append three columns to the feature matrix: RDKit Crippen MolLogP, TPSA and the count of hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors combined. Compute them from the same mol objects used for descriptors, cache per SMILES as desc_vector does, and clip to the 1st to 99th percentile range like the other descriptors. Keep these columns inside the LightGBM and RF inputs only, so the Tanimoto and RBF kernels still use the same columns as before. This is a small, cheap addition.

items.title: L1-optimal non-negative meta-learner
items.spec: Replace the Ridge(alpha=1e-3, positive=True) meta-learner with a non-negative least-absolute-deviation fit. Solve min over w >= 0 of sum |oof @ w - y| using scipy.optimize.linprog, with slack variables for the absolute residuals, and then add an intercept term fixed at zero. Use the L1-optimal weights for the final combination of base_te. Keep the oof matrix and the rest of the stack unchanged. The metric is MAE, so this aligns the meta-learner with the scoring.

items.title: Snapshot averaging of the LightGBM member
items.spec: Inside base_predict, train the LightGBM model once for N_ROUNDS and record its predictions at several checkpoints, for example rounds 300, 400, 500 and 600, using m.predict(Xb, num_iteration=k). Average these snapshot predictions to form p_lgb in place of the single final-round prediction. This adds no extra training cost, only extra predict calls. Keep the learning rate and all other parameters unchanged.

items.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour regression member
items.spec: Add a fourth column to base_predict's output: a similarity-weighted kNN regressor on the ECFP Tanimoto matrix. For each test molecule, take the k=10 training neighbours with the highest Tanimoto similarity (use the existing tanimoto(Fb, Fa) matrix) and predict the weighted mean of their targets with weights equal to similarity raised to the power 3. Fall back to the training mean when the top similarity is zero. Include the new column in the stack's oof matrix so that the Ridge meta-learner weighs it alongside the other three members.

items.title: Self-distillation of training targets
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, after the first oof stack pass, form soft targets y_s = 0.5 * y + 0.5 * oof_meta, where oof_meta is the meta-learner prediction on the out-of-fold matrix. Refit the whole stack once with y_s as the training target for base_predict in each fold, while the meta-learner is still fit against the original y. Final test predictions come from the refit base learners combined with the same meta weights. This is one extra pass through the stack, so reduce the inner Tanimoto grid if the job approaches the time limit.

items.title: Isotonic recalibration of the stacked output
items.spec: After meta.predict on the oof matrix, fit sklearn.isotonic.IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip') from the oof stacked predictions to y using only the out-of-fold data. Apply that isotonic map to the test-time stacked prediction before returning. This corrects any monotone bias the linear meta-learner leaves, such as compression at the extremes of logD. Keep the Ridge meta-learner as the first stage, and do not change the base learners.

items.title: Scaffold-frequency sample weighting
items.spec: Compute a weight for each training molecule from how common its Murcko scaffold is within the training fold: w_i = 1 / sqrt(count of molecules sharing its scaffold). Normalise the weights to mean 1. Pass them as sample_weight to the random forest fit and as the weight argument to lgb.Dataset in base_predict. Leave the kernel members unweighted, because the Tanimoto solve has no natural weight hook. The aim is to reduce the influence of large scaffold families on the trees.

items.title: Ionizable-group SMARTS count features
items.spec: logD depends strongly on ionization, so add a small block of substructure counts to the feature matrix. Define about 10 SMARTS patterns: carboxylic acid [CX3](=O)[OX2H1,OX1-], tetrazole, acyl sulfonamide, phenol, aliphatic primary/secondary/tertiary amines (non-amide, non-aniline N with sp3 carbons), amidine/guanidine, pyridine-type aromatic N, and quaternary N. In featurize (or a helper called from fit_predict), compute per-molecule counts with Chem.MolFromSmiles(s).GetSubstructMatches for each pattern and hstack them as float32 columns after the descriptor block. Keep the Tanimoto kernel on the ECFP bits only, as now, and make sure the base_predict slicing for descriptors (Xa[:, 2*N_BITS:]) is updated so the new columns are included in the RBF kernel and the tree models.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints at radius 3
items.spec: Replace the binary ECFP/FCFP bit vectors with hashed count vectors. Use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=3, fpSize=N_BITS) and call GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy for both the ECFP and FCFP generators in featurize, instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy. Counts carry occupancy information that bit vectors lose, which helps tree models on logD. For the Tanimoto kernel, switch to the count-based (min/max) Tanimoto: sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)), computed with a vectorized approach on the float64 ECFP count matrix, or keep the existing bit-based Tanimoto if the min/max version is too slow. Keep everything else unchanged.

items.title: Add MACCS keys to the feature matrix
items.spec: Append the 167-bit MACCS structural keys as an extra block: from rdkit.Chem import MACCSkeys, then for each molecule use np.array(MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys(mol), dtype=np.float32) (or GetFingerprintAsNumPy on the returned ExplicitBitVect). Compute it inside featurize alongside the Morgan fingerprints and hstack it after the existing fingerprint columns and before the descriptor block. Because base_predict slices descriptors as Xa[:, 2*N_BITS:], update that slice index to 2*N_BITS + 167 so the descriptors are still the block passed to the RBF kernel. The Tanimoto kernel should remain on the ECFP bits only.

items.title: CatBoost base learner with MAE loss
items.spec: Add a fourth base learner in base_predict: a CatBoostRegressor with loss_function='MAE', iterations=800, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0, trained on Xa and ya, predicting Xb. Return it as an extra column in the np.column_stack output, so the oof matrix in fit_predict becomes 4 columns wide (change np.zeros((len(y), 3)) to 4). Watch the time budget: the nested stacking calls base_predict 6 times per fit, so keep CatBoost fast (for example depth 6 and about 800 iterations on 3360 rows). If the total job time nears 10 minutes, drop the CatBoost iterations to 500.

items.title: Tanimoto kNN regressor as a base learner
items.spec: Add a nearest-neighbour base learner that uses the existing Tanimoto matrix. In base_predict, compute S = tanimoto(Fb, Fa) (already available as a helper, and it is cheap). For each row of Xb, take the k=7 most similar training molecules by S, and predict the similarity-weighted mean of ya over those neighbours, with weights S**2 and a small epsilon in the denominator. Return this as an extra column, and update the oof column count in fit_predict from 3 to 4 accordingly. Use argsort on -S, or np.argpartition for speed. This gives the stacker a local-similarity signal that differs from the kernel ridge fit.

items.title: Lower learning rate with more rounds for LightGBM
items.spec: Reduce the LightGBM learning rate from 0.03 to 0.01 and raise num_boost_round from N_ROUNDS=600 to 1500, which usually gives a smoother L1 fit with the same capacity. Change the constant N_ROUNDS to 1500 and the learning_rate in lgb_params to 0.01. Keep num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=10, feature_fraction=0.2. Check that the job stays under the 10-minute limit; if it does not, use 1000 rounds at learning_rate 0.015 instead.

items.title: Seed-bagged LightGBM for variance reduction
items.spec: Reduce the variance of the LightGBM base learner by averaging several models trained with different seeds. In base_predict, replace the single lgb.train call with a loop over 3 seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with its own lgb_params(...) and bagging_fraction=0.8 and bagging_freq=1 added to the params so the models differ. Average the predictions on Xb and return the mean as p_lgb. This keeps the same stacking interface and only changes how p_lgb is produced.

items.title: Huber objective for the LightGBM learner
items.spec: Change the LightGBM objective from regression_l1 to huber with alpha (the delta parameter) set to about 0.5, since logD targets have a range of roughly -1.5 to 4.5 and outliers are common. In lgb_params, set objective='huber' and add alpha=0.5. Huber gives smooth gradients near zero and robustness to outliers. Keep all other settings the same. Also try a second variant with objective='fair' and fair_c=0.5 if the first is not clearly better, but ship only the better one.

items.title: Non-negative averaging instead of positive Ridge meta-learner
items.spec: Simplify the stacking step. Replace meta = Ridge(alpha=1e-3, positive=True).fit(oof, y) with a constrained average: solve for non-negative weights summing to 1 by minimizing mean absolute error on the out-of-fold matrix oof against y, using scipy.optimize.minimize with method='SLSQP' and bounds [0,1], constraint sum(w)=1, starting from equal weights. Predict as base_te @ w. This removes the intercept and the free scale, which may overfit less with a small number of base learners, and matches the MAE objective used by the score. Remove the Ridge import if it is no longer used.

items.title: More regularized random forest
items.spec: The random forest base learner is currently RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=200, max_features=0.3, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) with min_samples_leaf defaulting to 1. Set min_samples_leaf=3 and max_features=0.2 so that leaves are smoother and each tree sees fewer features, which often generalizes better across unseen scaffolds. Also set max_samples=0.8 to add bootstrap-style subsampling diversity. Keep n_estimators=200. This is a one-line change to the constructor in base_predict and does not alter the interface.

items.title: RBF gamma scale grid for kernel ridge
items.spec: In base_predict, make the RBF bandwidth tunable: add a gamma multiplier g in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) applied to the current gamma=1/(2*n_desc). Compute Ra for each g once (3 dense matrices) and extend the inner GroupKFold grid over (lam, wr, g), keeping the 4-fold inner CV. Use the best triple for the final solve and the test kernel. Watch runtime: precompute the kernels outside the loops.

items.title: Salt stripping and neutralisation before featurising
items.spec: Add a helper that parses each SMILES, keeps the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), and neutralises charges (rdMolStandardize.Uncharger). Use the cleaned molecule in both featurize and desc_vector (cache key stays the original SMILES). Fall back to the original molecule if cleaning fails. Scaffold groups stay computed from the original SMILES.

items.title: Multi-seed averaging of tree base learners
items.spec: In base_predict, train the RandomForest and LightGBM with 3 different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2). For LightGBM also use bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1. Average each learner's predictions over the seeds before they enter the stack. Reduce RF to 150 trees per seed to keep the runtime similar. The kernel member stays unchanged.

items.title: L1-optimal meta-learner
items.spec: Replace the Ridge(positive=True) meta-learner with a non-negative weight vector that sums to 1 and minimises the mean absolute error on the out-of-fold predictions. Use scipy.optimize.minimize with a softmax parametrisation, or SLSQP with bounds and a sum constraint, started from equal weights. Predict with the weighted sum of base_te columns. Include no intercept.

items.title: Kernel ridge with mixed multi-radius Tanimoto
items.spec: In the kernel member, replace the ECFP Tanimoto kernel with the mean of Tanimoto kernels on ECFP bits (radius 2) and on count-based Morgan features using the min/max (generalised Tanimoto) kernel. Compute count features with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy at radius 3, 1024 bits, in featurize, stored as an extra array passed through. The kernel is sum_i min(a_i,b_i) / sum_i max(a_i,b_i), computed in chunks to bound memory. Keep the RBF term and the grid search.

items.title: Winsorise extreme training targets
items.spec: At the start of fit_predict, clip train_y to its 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles (computed on the training fold only) before fitting everything. Predictions are not clipped. This reduces the influence of outlier labels on the kernel ridge and the trees.

items.title: Subagged stack with median aggregate
items.spec: In fit_predict, after computing the meta-learner and base_te once on the full training set, also run the whole base_predict on 4 extra bootstrap-by-scaffold-group resamples (sample groups with replacement, seed-driven). Reuse the same meta weights. Return the median of the 5 stack predictions. Cap the runtime by skipping the inner stacking OOF for the resamples, since the meta weights are reused.

items.title: Gaussian-process style kernel member with learned noise via marginal likelihood
items.spec: Replace the grid search over lam and wr in base_predict with selection by log marginal likelihood. For each (lam, wr) in a 5x5 grid, take the eigendecomposition of Ta + wr*Ra once per wr. Compute the log marginal likelihood cheaply from the eigenvalues, with the targets centred. Choose the best pair and solve once. This removes the inner CV loops and so is faster. Optionally use the saved time to add more wr values.

items.title: Cosine-decayed learning rate for LightGBM
items.spec: In the stack's LightGBM member, train 900 rounds with a learning rate that decays from 0.06 to 0.01 along a cosine curve. Implement it with lgb.reset_parameter(learning_rate=lambda i: ...) passed as a callback. Keep the other parameters unchanged.

items.title: Generic-scaffold target-encoding feature
items.spec: Compute the generic Murcko scaffold (MakeScaffoldGeneric) for each molecule. Inside base_predict, for the tree learners only, add one column: the out-of-fold smoothed mean of y for the molecule's generic scaffold. Use smoothing m=5 toward the global mean. For training rows, compute it by leave-one-group-out using the Murcko scaffold groups ga. For test rows, use the full-training statistics. Unseen scaffolds get the global mean. Pass the generic scaffold strings through as an extra argument.

items.title: Add CatBoost base learner
items.spec: In base_predict, add a CatBoostRegressor (loss_function='MAE', iterations=800, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, thread_count=8, random_seed=seed, verbose=0) fit on Xa (fingerprints plus descriptors) and append its predictions as a 4th column. Change oof to have 4 columns (np.zeros((len(y), 4))). The positive-ridge meta learner then weights it.

items.title: Count-based Morgan features
items.spec: In featurize, use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy (count simulation) instead of binary GetFingerprintAsNumPy for both ECFP and FCFP, so the tree models see substructure counts. Keep the Tanimoto kernel input binary by thresholding Ftr[:, :N_BITS] > 0 before casting, or use the min/max Tanimoto on counts.

items.title: Add atom-pair and RDKit path fingerprints
items.spec: Extend featurize with 1024-bit count atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator) and 1024-bit topological-torsion fingerprints. Concatenate them before the descriptor block. Update the descriptor slicing, which currently uses 2*N_BITS, to use a constant N_FP equal to the total fingerprint width.

items.title: Crippen/MolLogP-residual target
items.spec: Compute Crippen MolLogP for each molecule. Train the base models on y - a*logP, where a comes from a linear fit of y on logP over the training fold. Add it back at prediction. Do this inside base_predict, or simply give the models a lower-variance target. Keep the descriptors as features.

items.title: Larger KRR hyperparameter grid with MinMax kernel
items.spec: Replace the binary Tanimoto kernel with the count-based MinMax kernel on count Morgan (radius 3) vectors. Widen the lam grid to (0.03,0.1,0.3,1.0) and the wr grid to (0.25,0.5,1,2,4). Check whether the KRR column improves the ensemble.

items.title: Multi-seed RF and LGB averaging
items.spec: In base_predict, average 3 LightGBM models trained with seeds seed, seed+1 and seed+2 (use bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1 for diversity). Raise the RF to 400 trees with min_samples_leaf=1 and max_features=0.2. This reduces variance in the base predictions fed to the meta learner.

items.title: LightGBM tuning: lower LR, more rounds, stronger regularization
items.spec: Set the LGB learning_rate to 0.02 and N_ROUNDS to 1200. Add lambda_l2=5, min_child_samples=15, feature_fraction=0.15, and use the huber objective (alpha=1.0) instead of regression_l1. Keep the rest unchanged and check the time budget.

items.title: Add an MLP base learner
items.spec: Add sklearn MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(256,64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, max_iter=300, random_state=seed). Train it on the standardized descriptors Za and the first 1024 ECFP bits, and average 3 seeds. Add its predictions as an extra column in base_predict and make oof 4 columns wide.

items.title: Extra RDKit descriptors: MQN and fragment counts
items.spec: Append rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_ (42 features), Crippen per-atom-type contributions via rdMolDescriptors, and the counts of the 2D pharmacophore feature types to desc_vector. Cache them as before. They then go through the same percentile clipping and feed all models.

items.title: Nonnegative meta stacker with bias and CV-selected shrinkage
items.spec: Replace the Ridge(positive=True) meta learner with a stacker fit on the out-of-fold predictions that minimizes MAE. Use scipy.optimize.minimize over simplex weights (softmax parametrization) on the L1 loss of the OOF predictions. This matches the MAE metric and avoids the 1e-3 ridge shrinkage.

items.title: Median-heuristic RBF bandwidth in the kernel member
items.spec: In base_predict, the descriptor RBF kernel currently uses a fixed gamma = 1.0 / (2 * d) where d is the number of descriptor columns. Replace this with the median heuristic: after z-scoring the descriptor block, draw a subsample of at most 1000 training rows with rng = np.random.default_rng(seed), compute the pairwise squared Euclidean distances within that subsample, take the median of the strictly off-diagonal entries, and set gamma = 1.0 / median_sq_dist. Use that gamma inside rbf() for both the train-train kernel and the test-train kernel. Everything else (the lambda and RBF-weight grid search, the RF and LightGBM members, the Ridge meta-learner) stays exactly as it is. The bandwidth is then matched to the actual scale of the data instead of a dimension-based guess, and the cost is negligible.

items.title: Eigendecomposition sweep over a wider kernel-ridge lambda grid
items.spec: The kernel-ridge member currently grid-searches lambda in (0.1, 0.5, 2.0) and RBF weight in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) using one np.linalg.solve per combination per inner fold. Restructure this so that for each RBF weight and each inner GroupKFold(n_splits=4) split, the combined kernel K = Ta[itr,itr] + wr * Ra[itr,itr] is factorised once with np.linalg.eigh giving eigenvalues s and vectors U, and then every lambda is evaluated in closed form as w_in = U @ ((U.T @ (y_tr - mu)) / (s + lam)). Because one eigendecomposition serves all lambdas, widen the grid to lam in (0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0) at roughly the current runtime. Select (lam, wr) by summed absolute validation error as now, then refit on the full training block with np.linalg.solve as before. No other part of the script changes.

items.title: Rank-Gauss transform of descriptors before the RBF kernel
items.spec: The descriptor block feeding the RBF kernel is currently only mean/std standardised, so heavy-tailed columns such as molecular weight, Ipc and various counts dominate Euclidean distances. In base_predict, replace that standardisation with sklearn.preprocessing.QuantileTransformer(n_quantiles=min(1000, n_train), output_distribution='normal', random_state=seed), fitted on the training descriptor rows and applied to both train and test rows. Afterwards drop any column whose standard deviation is below 1e-9, and keep gamma = 1.0 / (2 * n_remaining_columns). Only the kernel member is affected; the random forest and LightGBM members keep the existing clipped raw descriptors, and the stacking structure is unchanged.

items.title: Replicate the incumbent to confirm its loss
items.spec: Make no change to train.py at all and run the current script as a job. The incumbent loss of 0.4895 rests on a single run and the noise standard deviation per job is about 0.0042, so several of the recent small-delta rejections were decided against an estimate that itself carries roughly that much uncertainty. A second measurement halves the standard error of the incumbent and makes the accept/reject threshold for subsequent ideas much more reliable. If the two runs disagree by more than about 0.01, treat the incumbent as unconfirmed and prefer future candidates with larger deltas.

items.title: Non-negative L1 meta-learner via linear programming
items.spec: The stack's meta-learner is a Ridge with positive=True and alpha=1e-3, which minimises squared error even though the harness scores mean absolute error. Replace it with a direct L1 fit: solve min over w >= 0 and intercept b of sum_i |y_i - (b + w . oof_i)| using scipy.optimize.linprog with the standard epigraph formulation (one slack variable per training row, two inequality constraints per row, bounds that keep the weights non-negative and the intercept free, method='highs'). Apply the fitted weights and intercept to the base-learner predictions on the test set. If linprog fails to converge, fall back to the existing Ridge. The number of base columns is three, so the program is small and fast.

items.title: Multi-seed averaging of the stochastic base learners
items.spec: Both the random forest and the LightGBM member are stochastic, and a single draw adds variance on top of the genuine model error. Inside base_predict, fit each of them three times with random_state / seed values seed, seed + 1000 and seed + 2000, and average the three prediction vectors into a single column before returning. To stay inside the ten-minute limit, drop the random forest to 120 trees and LightGBM to 400 rounds so the total tree count is roughly unchanged. The kernel-ridge member is deterministic given its grid search and is left untouched, as is the stacking loop and the meta-learner.

items.title: Salt stripping and charge neutralisation before featurising
items.spec: Several entries in this kind of data set are salts or charged forms, so the same parent molecule can produce different fingerprints and descriptors. Add a cached helper that, for each SMILES, parses the molecule, keeps only the largest fragment by heavy-atom count (split on '.' or use rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags), then neutralises the common ionised groups by applying rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and returns the canonical SMILES of the result. Route every call that currently does Chem.MolFromSmiles -- in featurize, desc_vector and the Murcko scaffold computation -- through this cleaned structure. Cache per input SMILES because the same molecules recur across the fifteen fits. If standardisation raises for a molecule, fall back to the original parse.

items.title: Scaffold-group bagged ensemble of the whole stack
items.spec: Wrap fit_predict's final test-time fit in a bagging loop over scaffold groups. Build the Murcko scaffold group array as now, then for each of five repeats with rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + repeat), sample the unique scaffold groups with replacement, take all rows belonging to the sampled groups as the bag, call base_predict on that bag to predict the test molecules, apply the already-fitted meta-learner weights, and store the result. Return the median of the five resulting prediction vectors. To keep inside the time limit, reduce the inner out-of-fold stacking loop that produces the meta-learner's training matrix from five folds to three. Sampling whole scaffolds rather than rows keeps the resampling aligned with how the harness splits data.

items.title: Transductive pseudo-label self-training round
items.spec: Add one round of self-training at the end of fit_predict. After computing the test predictions in the usual way, form an augmented training set consisting of the real training rows plus the test rows carrying their predicted values as pseudo-labels, with sample weights 1.0 for real rows and 0.3 for pseudo-labelled rows. Refit only the LightGBM and random-forest base learners on this augmented set (pass the weights through sample_weight and LightGBM's weight argument), leaving the kernel member and the meta-learner weights from the first pass unchanged, and recombine with the same meta-learner coefficients to give the final predictions. Guard the whole second pass in a try/except that returns the first-pass predictions on any failure, and keep the extra fit cheap enough that total runtime stays well under ten minutes.

items.title: Out-of-fold isotonic recalibration of the stacked prediction
items.spec: The stack already produces an out-of-fold matrix of base predictions for every training molecule. Use it to correct any systematic bias in the final output: apply the fitted meta-learner to the out-of-fold matrix to obtain one out-of-fold stacked prediction per training molecule, then fit sklearn.isotonic.IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip', increasing=True) mapping those out-of-fold predictions to the true targets, and pass the test-set stacked predictions through the fitted isotonic map before returning them. Because the calibrator is fitted on scaffold-grouped out-of-fold values it cannot leak within-fold information. Keep the uncalibrated prediction as a fallback if the isotonic fit raises.

items.title: Count Morgan fingerprints + MinMax kernel
items.spec: In featurize, use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy for both the ECFP and FCFP generators, and clip counts at 255 (float32). The tree models then see counts. In base_predict, replace the tanimoto() kernel on Fa/Fb with the MinMax (generalized Tanimoto) kernel: K(a,b)=sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)). Compute it memory-efficiently by looping over chunks of 256 rows of A (np.minimum(A_chunk[:,None,:],B[None,:,:]).sum(-1) is too large for 1024 columns, so instead use the identity sum(max)=sum(a)+sum(b)-sum(min). Compute sum(min) by expanding counts into thresholded binary planes: for t in 1..max_count (cap at 8 by clipping counts at 8 for the kernel only), sum(min)=sum_t (A>=t)@(B>=t).T). Everything else stays unchanged.

items.title: Add CatBoost as fourth base learner
items.spec: In base_predict, add a fourth base learner: catboost.CatBoostRegressor(iterations=800, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, loss_function='MAE', rsm=0.2, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0), fit on Xa, ya and predict Xb. Append p_cb as a fourth column of the returned matrix, and change oof = np.zeros((len(y), 3)) to np.zeros((len(y), 4)). The positive Ridge meta-learner stays. If runtime gets near the limit, reduce iterations to 500.

items.title: Residual learning on Crippen logP
items.spec: Use calculated logP as a physics prior. In fit_predict, compute c = Crippen.MolLogP for each train and test molecule (from rdkit.Chem import Crippen; cache per SMILES like the descriptors). Fit a 1-D Huber regression (sklearn HuberRegressor) of y on c over the training set to get a, b, and set the baseline to base = a*c + b. Run the whole existing pipeline (OOF stacking, base_predict, meta) on the residual target r = y - base_tr instead of y, then return meta.predict(base_te) + base_te_prior, where base_te_prior = a*c_te + b. Features are unchanged.

items.title: Multi-fingerprint kernel for KRR
items.spec: Extend the KRR base learner's kernel with an atom-pair fingerprint Tanimoto term. In fit_predict, also compute 1024-bit atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024), GetFingerprintAsNumPy) for train and test as float64 arrays Atr, Ate (not added to the tree features). Pass them through to base_predict, slicing them like Ftr/Fte. In base_predict, use kernel K = T_ecfp + T_ap + wr*RBF, where T_ap = tanimoto(Aa, Aa) and tanimoto(Ab, Aa) for prediction. Keep the existing grid search over lam and wr. Use the same changes in both the inner CV and the final solve.

items.title: Stronger LightGBM: slower lr, bagging, seed average
items.spec: In lgb_params, set learning_rate=0.02 and add bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1, lambda_l2=1.0. Set N_ROUNDS=1200. In base_predict, train the LightGBM model with 3 seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) and average their predictions into p_lgb. Leave every other part unchanged. If the job approaches the 10-minute limit, use 2 seeds instead.

items.title: Replace RF with ExtraTrees on min_samples_leaf=2
items.spec: In base_predict, replace the RandomForestRegressor with sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=300, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed). ExtraTrees usually extrapolates more smoothly on fingerprint plus descriptor features and is faster. Nothing else changes.

items.title: MAE meta-learner with intercept
items.spec: The metric is MAE but the stacker minimizes squared error. Replace meta = Ridge(alpha=1e-3, positive=True).fit(oof, y) with an L1 meta-learner: sklearn.linear_model.QuantileRegressor(quantile=0.5, alpha=0.0, solver='highs').fit(oof, y). Then clip negative coefficients to zero: if any coef_ < 0, refit on only the columns with positive weights (keep a column mask and apply it to base_te at predict time). Return meta.predict(base_te[:, mask]).

items.title: Radius-3 ECFP with 2048 bits
items.spec: Change the settings to N_BITS = 2048 and RADIUS = 3. Since the code slices descriptors as Xa[:, 2*N_BITS:] and the kernel uses Ftr[:, :N_BITS], those slices update automatically. Larger substructures and fewer bit collisions should help both the Tanimoto KRR and the trees. Make no other change. If runtime is too long, lower RF n_estimators from 200 to 150.

items.title: Add MACCS keys and descriptor-only SVR
items.spec: Add the 167 MACCS keys (from rdkit.Chem import MACCSkeys; np.array(MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys(mol)), cached per SMILES) as a separate block. Append it to Xtr/Xte after the descriptor block, and in base_predict change the descriptor slice to Xa[:, 2*N_BITS:2*N_BITS+n_desc] (pass n_desc = len(Descriptors._descList)). Also add a fourth base learner: sklearn.svm.SVR(C=5.0, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') fit on the standardized descriptor block Za concatenated with the MACCS block. Its prediction is a fourth column, and oof gets 4 columns.

items.title: Cheaper KRR search, reused for final fit
items.spec: The KRR hyperparameter grid search runs inside every outer stacking fold plus the final fit, which costs a lot of time. Run the (lam, wr) grid search only once per fit_predict call, on the full training set with the existing GroupKFold(4) over scaffold groups. Pass the chosen (lam, wr) into base_predict as an argument and remove the search from base_predict. Use the saved time to widen the grid to lam in (0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0) and wr in (0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0). Predictions otherwise stay the same.
